# Results — Study 732 (Tour-de-France-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **French
equities enjoy a feel-good July "Grande Boucle" seasonal** while the country watches the
Tour de France — the summer-holiday cousin of sports-sentiment folklore, recast as a
three-week *calendar window* on the CAC / EWQ. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `bf542dd5cb07` (EWQ + `^FCHI` + VGK, one combined
panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes: `EWQ` (iShares MSCI France, **total-return**) + `^FCHI` (CAC 40, **price-only**, dividends NOT reinvested) + `VGK` (Vanguard FTSE Europe, total-return), one combined panel: 9,328 rows, 1990-03-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 30 Tour de France editions 1996→2025, Grand Départ + final-stage date per year (Wikipedia "List of Tour de France editions" + per-year race pages) |
| Editions resolvable | all **30** covered by EWQ (raw seasonal); **21** (2005→2025) also covered by VGK for the France-minus-Europe *abnormal* test; window length 15–16 sessions (mean 15.5) |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known window, so no information lag** — the Tour dates are public a year ahead. Entry = last close before the Grand Départ; exit = first close on/after the final stage (the Champs-Élysées Sunday is non-trading). Signal = gross window return; Tradability = same window net of 2× one-way cost × NAV |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the window return across independent, non-overlapping annual editions (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo; raw-vs-abnormal decomposition for the summer-beta third axis |
| Data quirks (named) | **2020** was pushed by COVID-19 from July to **Aug 29 → Sep 20** — its window is measured on the *actual race dates* (a natural "does the effect follow the race or the calendar?" probe); **2024** finished in Nice, not Paris (Paris Olympics) — no market consequence |

**Price-only vs total-return, labelled:** `EWQ` and `VGK` are total-return (dividends
reinvested); `^FCHI` (CAC 40) is a **price index** with no dividend reinvestment and is
used only as a long-history cross-check on the raw seasonal — it *understates* true French
equity returns and is never mixed into the total-return abnormal test.

## The raw seasonal — EWQ total return over the Tour window (entry → exit)

| cut | n | mean | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| EWQ raw (1996–2025) | 30 | **−0.347%** | **−0.37** | 13/30 = 43.3% [27.4%, 60.8%] |
| EWQ raw, net @ 5 bps | 30 | −0.447% | −0.48 | 13/30 = 43.3% [27.4%, 60.8%] |
| CAC 40 (price-only) | 30 | −0.325% | −0.38 | 18/30 = 60.0% [42.3%, 75.4%] |

The "feel-good bump" is, on average, a **mild drag**: buy French equities for the three
weeks of the Tour and you are down ~0.35% before costs, ~0.45% after. The hit rate is
*below* a coin flip (13/30). That is not a surprise once you remember the Tour runs in
**July** — squarely inside the "Sell in May and go away" summer-weakness window.

## The abnormal (France-specific) — EWQ minus VGK Europe, same window (2005 →)

| series (2005+ subset) | n | mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| EWQ France | 21 | +0.476% | +0.42 |
| VGK Europe (the summer-doldrums component, shared region-wide) | 21 | +0.681% | +0.66 |
| **abnormal (France − Europe)** | 21 | **−0.205%** | **−0.78** |

This is the decisive cut. Over the VGK era France does **not** beat Europe during the Tour
— it slightly *lags* (abnormal −0.205%, *t* = −0.78, hit 9/21). Whatever the July window
does, France does it *because it is part of Europe*, not because of any home-crowd Tour
effect. The unpaired Welch *t* (France − Europe) is −0.13. **There is no France-specific
signal to find.**

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws; same-length windows elsewhere in the tape)

| cut | observed | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| raw, left-tail (as weak or weaker) | −0.347% | +0.586% (0.961%) | 0.167 |
| raw net @ 5 bps, left-tail | −0.447% | +0.486% (0.961%) | 0.167 |
| abnormal, left-tail | −0.205% | −0.019% (0.270%) | 0.247 |
| raw, right-tail (share of ordinary windows that **beat** the Tour mean) | | | 0.833 |
| abnormal, right-tail | | | 0.752 |

An ordinary three-week EWQ window averages **+0.59%** (equities drift up); the Tour window
averages −0.35% — about 0.9% below the typical window, consistent with summer softness, but
comfortably *inside* the luck cloud (left-tail *p* = 0.167). Read the other way: **83% of
random windows beat the Tour window** — it is a below-median but entirely unremarkable
three weeks, not a special date on the calendar.

## Event anatomy — mean cumulative return by session offset from entry

| session | 0 | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| raw (EWQ) | 0.000% | −0.486% | −0.208% | −0.451% | −0.250% |
| abnormal (EWQ − VGK) | 0.000% | −0.175% | −0.303% | −0.223% | −0.271% |

No pop, no drift, no shape at all — the path wanders around zero-to-slightly-negative for
the whole race. There is no broadcast-driven reaction here to find (contrast study 708's
one honestly-surprising winner/1-month cut, or study 637's clean FOMC vol crush).

## Robustness — the 2020 "calendar vs race" probe

The 2020 Tour was pushed by COVID-19 from July to **Aug 29 → Sep 20**, so its window is
the study's cleanest test of whether any "effect" tracks the *race* or the *calendar
month*. It doesn't matter: 2020's actual-window return (raw **−5.03%**, abnormal −0.96%)
is simply a bad market month, the worst single edition, and **dropping it entirely leaves
the verdict unchanged** — raw mean −0.185%, *t* = −0.19 over the remaining 29 editions.
Nothing hinges on it either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (France, Europe) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.85, like a single-country
ETF vs its regional benchmark) with a scheduled annual window and a TUNABLE planted
per-day "July bump"; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.44** (sd 0.83), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted +5 bp/day (seed 732) | **+3.38** |
| planted +10 bp/day (seed 732) | **+5.41** |

The detector recovers a planted seasonal cleanly and never fires on the null across 20
seeds — the machinery works; the real-tape story is genuinely this empty. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The raw July seasonal is a mild *negative* (−0.347%, *t* = −0.37),
  the France-specific abnormal return is also *negative* (−0.205%, *t* = −0.78), and
  neither is distinguishable from an ordinary three-week window (placebo *p* = 0.167 /
  0.247). The hit rate is below a coin flip. There is nothing here, in either direction, at
  any of the desk's bars.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no positive edge to trade — the seasonal is negative
  before costs and more negative after (−0.447% net @ 5 bps). "Buy French stocks during
  the Tour" is a systematic small *loss*, i.e. paying spread to rent the summer doldrums.
- **A France-specific effect? — NOT SUPPORTED.** France does not outperform Europe during
  the Tour (it slightly lags; Welch *t* = −0.13). The mild July softness is ordinary
  pan-European summer beta, not a home-crowd sentiment bump — the folklore mis-attributes a
  region-wide, calendar-driven non-event to a bike race.
